name: LAOS

flag.title: Flag of Laos
flag.note: Red, blue, red — white disc for unity

lead: Laos is a forested country in Southeast Asia. It is the only one in the region with no coast. The Mekong River flows along its western edge past rice paddies and temple towns. Wild elephants wade through jungle rivers.

facts.label: Area
facts.sub: A bit bigger than the UK

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Nearly three-quarters of Laos is steep mountain and thick jungle. The cool Bolaven Plateau is famous for coffee and waterfalls. At Kuang Si, water tumbles over white limestone into turquoise pools.
The Mekong runs 1,835 km along the western border. In the south, Si Phan Don means 'Four Thousand Islands'. You can watch the river drift past from a hammock.
animals: Laos was called the Land of a Million Elephants. Around 700 Asian elephants still roam its forests. Moon bears, clouded leopards and the unicorn-like saola hide in the Annamite mountains.
The Mekong once held sacred Irrawaddy dolphins. The last one in Laos died in 2022. Giant Mekong catfish, up to 300 kg, still lurk in deep pools.
culture: People in Laos eat more sticky rice than anyone on Earth, about 171 kg a year each. Meals are shared, with fish, herbs and papaya salad called som tam.
Buddhism shapes daily life. At sunrise in Luang Prabang, hundreds of monks in saffron robes walk silently through the streets to collect rice. This ritual is called Tak Bat.
history: The kingdom of Lan Xang, 'Million Elephants', began in 1353. It once stretched from the Yunnan border to Cambodia. Luang Prabang was its gilded capital.
France colonised Laos in 1893. Laos gained independence in 1953. Between 1964 and 1973, the US secretly dropped over two million tonnes of bombs. A third never exploded and still hurts people.
wows: Laos is Southeast Asia's only landlocked country.
Laos is the most bombed country per person in history.
Stone jars on the Plain of Jars weigh up to 14 tonnes.
Laotians eat 171 kg of sticky rice a year, a world record.
No scientist has ever seen a live saola in the wild.
Landlocked Laos has Si Phan Don, the 'Four Thousand Islands'.
Pha That Luang in Vientiane is covered in real gold.

myths.myth: Laos is always hot and tropical
myths.fact: Highland towns like Phonsavan drop near freezing in winter.
Elephants suck water up into the trunk. Then they squirt it into their mouths.
